output.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(net_revenue) FILTER (WHERE order_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND order_date < DATE '2025-01-01') AS rev_2024,
    SUM(net_revenue) FILTER (WHERE order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND order_date < DATE '2026-01-01') AS rev_2025
  FROM marts.fct_orders
  WHERE is_revenue
)
SELECT
  ROUND(rev_2024, 2) AS revenue_2024,
  ROUND(rev_2025, 2) AS revenue_2025,
  ROUND((rev_2025 - rev_2024) / NULLIF(rev_2024, 0) * 100, 2) AS growth_pct
FROM yearly;
output.explanation: The query compares net revenue for fiscal 2024 and 2025. Fiscal years match calendar years. Only completed orders count (is_revenue = true), and shipping fees are left out. Growth is (2025 revenue − 2024 revenue) / 2024 revenue × 100, rounded to 2 decimals. It also returns both yearly totals for context. Keep in mind that list prices rose 4% on 2025-01-01, so part of the growth comes from higher prices rather than more sales.
